source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Nursing research is best defined as:
questions.rationale: Nursing research is disciplined, systematic inquiry that develops evidence for nursing practice.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 1 Summary (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: Nursing research is systematic inquiry undertaken to develop evidence on problems of importance to nurses.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A ward keeps turning patients every 2 hours "because we have always done it this way." This source of knowledge is:
questions.rationale: Tradition is knowledge passed on as custom; EBP replaces custom with research evidence.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 1 Summary (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: Disciplined research stands in contrast to other knowledge sources for nursing practice, such as tradition, authority, personal experience, and trial and error.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse reads a published study on kangaroo mother care and decides whether its findings apply to her ward. She is acting as a:
questions.rationale: Consumers read and evaluate studies; producers design and conduct them.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 1 Summary (PDF p. 53)
questions.quote: consumers of research (who read and evaluate studies) and producers of research (who design and undertake studies).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which paradigm assumes there is an objective reality that can be measured, and is linked with quantitative research?
questions.rationale: Positivism assumes an orderly, objective reality; constructivism holds that reality is constructed by people (qualitative).
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 1 Summary (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: In the positivist paradigm, it is assumed that there is an objective reality and that natural phenomena are regular and orderly.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A study collects mothers' stories about caring for a child with cancer in their own words. This research is:
questions.rationale: Qualitative research gathers subjective, narrative data to understand lived experience.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 1 Summary (PDF p. 54)
questions.quote: understanding human experience as it is lived through the collection and analysis of subjective, narrative materials

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Evidence-based practice integrates the best research evidence with:
questions.rationale: EBP combines current best evidence, the clinician's expertise and the patient's values and preferences.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 2 Summary (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: emphasizes the integration of research evidence with clinical expertise and patient preferences.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In most evidence hierarchies, the strongest evidence comes from:
questions.rationale: Systematic reviews of rigorous studies sit at the top of evidence hierarchies; opinion is at the bottom.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 2 Summary (PDF p. 81)
questions.quote: In all evidence hierarchies, however, systematic reviews are at the pinnacle.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: "Among postpartum mothers (P), does breastfeeding education (I) compared with routine care (C) increase exclusive breastfeeding (O)?" This question follows the:
questions.rationale: PICO stands for Population, Intervention, Comparison and Outcome, used to frame answerable clinical questions.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 2 Summary (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: population (P), intervention or influence (I), comparison (C), and outcome (O).

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: What is the first step a nurse takes in evidence-based practice?
questions.rationale: The steps are: ask a question, search for evidence, appraise and synthesize, integrate with other factors, assess effectiveness.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 2 Summary (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: The five basic steps for individual EBP are (1) asking an answerable clinical question

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A hospital's nursing service tracks its own fall rate and changes its bed-rail checks to reduce falls on its wards. This project is mainly:
questions.rationale: QI improves practices within a specific organization; it does not aim to produce generalizable knowledge.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 2 Summary (PDF p. 82)
questions.quote: The purpose of quality improvement (QI) is to improve practices and processes within a specific organization—not to generate new knowledge that can be generalized.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which framework is commonly used to guide quality improvement projects?
questions.rationale: QI uses PDSA (or PDCA) cycles to test and refine changes.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 325)
questions.quote: they often use a model called Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) or Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A study tests whether music therapy lowers anxiety before surgery. The dependent variable is:
questions.rationale: The dependent (outcome) variable is what is affected; the independent variable is the presumed cause (music therapy).
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: The dependent (or outcome) variable is the behavior, characteristic, or outcome the researcher is interested in explaining, predicting, or affecting

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In a study on the effect of a health teaching program on medication adherence, the health teaching program is the:
questions.rationale: The independent variable is the presumed cause or influence on the outcome.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: The independent variable is the presumed cause of or influence on the dependent variable.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A researcher defines pain as "the score on a 0–10 numeric rating scale." This is a(n):
questions.rationale: An operational definition specifies how a variable will be measured; a conceptual definition gives its abstract meaning.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: A conceptual definition describes the abstract meaning of a concept being studied. An operational definition specifies how the variable will be measured.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A researcher records the existing smoking habits and lung function of jeepney drivers without giving any intervention. This is:
questions.rationale: Nonexperimental (observational) research collects data on existing phenomena without intervening.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: nonexperimental (or observational) research, in which researchers collect data about existing phenomena without intervening.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nurse researcher wants to understand what it is like to live with a colostomy. Which qualitative tradition fits best?
questions.rationale: Phenomenology studies the lived experience of people; ethnography studies cultures; grounded theory studies social processes.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: Phenomenology focuses on the lived experiences of humans

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A study of the health beliefs and practices of an indigenous Aeta community, using long fieldwork and participant observation, is:
questions.rationale: Ethnography studies the meanings, patterns and lifeways of a culture holistically.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: Ethnography provides a framework for studying the meanings, patterns, and lifeways of a culture in a holistic fashion.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A researcher studies how new graduate nurses gradually adjust to hospital work and develops a theory from the data. This tradition is:
questions.rationale: Grounded theory develops theory inductively about social psychological processes.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 107)
questions.quote: Grounded theory seeks to describe and understand key social psychological processes that occur in a social setting.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which step belongs to the conceptual phase of a quantitative study?
questions.rationale: The conceptual phase includes defining the problem, reviewing literature, developing a framework and formulating hypotheses.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: developing a framework and conceptual definitions, and (5) formulating hypotheses to be tested.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In qualitative research, the researcher stops recruiting participants when:
questions.rationale: Sampling continues until saturation, when information becomes redundant.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: until saturation (redundancy of information) is achieved.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In a qualitative study in a rural health unit, the municipal health officer who must approve access to the site is called the:
questions.rationale: Researchers gain entrée to a site by enlisting the cooperation of gatekeepers.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 3 Summary (PDF p. 108)
questions.quote: researchers select a site and seek to gain entrée into it, which typically involves enlisting the cooperation of gatekeepers within the site.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In the IMRAD format of a research article, the section that explains what the findings mean and their implications is the:
questions.rationale: Introduction = problem; Method = strategies; Results = findings; Discussion = interpretation and implications.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 4 Summary (PDF p. 129)
questions.quote: Discussion (interpretation and implications of the findings).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The brief synopsis at the start of a research article is the:
questions.rationale: The abstract summarizes the study so readers can judge its relevance quickly.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 4 Summary (PDF p. 129)
questions.quote: Journal articles often consist of an abstract (a synopsis of the study)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A researcher uses interviews, observation and records to confirm the same finding. This strategy is:
questions.rationale: Triangulation uses multiple sources or methods to draw conclusions about the truth, enhancing credibility.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 4 Summary (PDF p. 129)
questions.quote: Triangulation, the use of multiple sources to draw conclusions about the truth, is one approach to enhancing credibility.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Neither the participants nor the data collectors know who received the new treatment. This is called:
questions.rationale: Blinding (masking) avoids bias from awareness of group assignment or hypotheses.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 4 Summary (PDF p. 130)
questions.quote: Blinding (or masking) is sometimes used to avoid biases stemming from participants’ or research agents’ awareness of study hypotheses or research status.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A qualitative researcher keeps a journal reflecting on how her own experiences as a mother may color her interpretation. This is:
questions.rationale: Reflexivity is critical self-reflection on values that could affect data collection and interpretation.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 4 Summary (PDF p. 130)
questions.quote: Reflexivity, the process of reflecting critically on the self and of scrutinizing personal values that could affect data collection and interpretation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The extent to which findings of a quantitative study apply to other groups and settings is its:
questions.rationale: Generalizability concerns applying findings beyond the sample; its qualitative counterpart is transferability.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 4 Summary (PDF p. 130)
questions.quote: Generalizability in a quantitative study concerns the extent to which the findings can be applied to other groups and settings.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In a study of exercise and blood pressure, participants' age could also affect blood pressure. Age here is a(n):
questions.rationale: Confounding (extraneous) variables are outside influences on the outcome that researchers try to control.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 4 Summary (PDF p. 130)
questions.quote: Researchers seek to control confounding (or extraneous) variables—variables that are extraneous to the purpose of a specific study.
